source.title: Memorization in image classification: test set behavior and scaling laws

record.tranche_reason: The paper directly tests random-label fitting and training dynamics in CIFAR-10 CNNs, while adding measures of test-set prediction disagreement and dataset-size effects.
record.gate_note: Reports its own CIFAR-10 results for true labels, random labels, and random-pixel inputs. Rows below cover stated outcomes in the text; figure-only condition-specific values are not reconstructed. Background statements citing prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures random-label and random-input memorization using CIFAR-10 CNNs trained with SGD and evaluated by training accuracy, extending the original experimental method with dataset-size, width, and optimization-policy comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors find initialization-dependent predictions away from memorized examples and fewer presentations per example when unrelated examples are added, including random-pixel inputs. Qualify the policy interpretation: batch size and learning rate change together, so their separate causal effects are not isolated.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 CNNs trained with SGD on random labels and random-pixel inputs, but focuses on test prediction disagreement, capacity frontiers, and dataset-size learning dynamics rather than reproducing the original memorization measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size and joint batch-size/learning-rate policy change memorization efficiency; random-pixel behavior is more policy-sensitive, and fraction-scaled random-pixel runs at larger fractions fail within the 100-epoch budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorizing models make confident, initialization-dependent predictions on unseen examples; random-label test predictions are uniform across initializations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models fitting identical arbitrary labels can agree on training examples while learning different predictive functions elsewhere.

fits_no_version.finding: Presentations per example can decrease as unrelated training examples are added, with dependence on the joint batch-size and learning-rate policy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization efficiency depends on dataset size and optimization policy even without shared input-label structure.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: Neural Network Artifacts as a New Data Modality
record.problems: Single-run configurations in the memorization-frontier experiment; random-pixel trajectories are irregular and may reflect stochastic variation; some random-pixel runs fail to reach thresholds within the 100-epoch budget. Predictive-dynamics results are described mostly qualitatively without exact numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-specific values by fraction, policy, or test-set condition are not transcribed because the supplied text does not state their numbers. Rows summarize only outcomes explicitly described in prose.

untested.parts: Increasing fractions of corrupted labels; direct constant-factor comparisons of time to zero training error. R4 instead compares time to 95% accuracy.
Shared pixel shuffling, independent pixel permutations, and explicitly Gaussian inputs. The study specifies independently sampled pixel arrays without naming their distribution.
The corruption-fraction sweep and its joint training-error and test-error trajectory.
Comparative effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization. Using no augmentation alone does not test the full claim.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels within training. Separate true-label and random-label learning curves do not establish that ordering.

missing.what: Random-label capacity-frontier results: insufficient-width models fail to interpolate within budget, and the required width grows with dataset size. Reported log-width versus log-size slopes are about 0.4 under the fixed policy and 0.35–0.48 under the scaled policy.

Matched predictive-dynamics ensemble execution times: true labels 52.2 minutes, random labels 90.8 minutes, approximately a 1.74-fold increase. These are aggregate experiment runtimes, not isolated optimization-step timings.
missing.locator: Appendix A.1; experimental settings in Appendix A.3

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Randomized-label experiments are eligible here because random-label fitting is itself the target claim. Missing numerical figure values are already declared in rows_left_out; no values were reconstructed. Descriptive fitted limits should not be treated as established asymptotic laws.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random labels on CIFAR-10 CNNs under the stated SGD settings; does not test other image datasets or network families.
Reports presentations per example and their dependence on dataset size, but does not compare a numeric constant-factor training-time ratio to true-label training.
Tests independently sampled random-pixel arrays, but does not test shuffled pixels or independently permuted pixels.
Does not sweep fractions of corrupted labels; random-label condition uses a fixed random assignment.
No weight-decay, dropout, or data-augmentation ablation is reported.
Does not measure whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: 4×-width CNN ensemble (20 independently initialized models)
rows.size_stated: three convolutional layers with 128/256/512 channels and a 1024-unit hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 natural images with fixed random training labels sampled uniformly from ten classes; evaluate train/test predictive behavior.
rows.measure: Training-set fit and test accuracy/prediction behavior
rows.baseline: true-label condition: disagreement remains low on training and test examples
rows.value: Models almost perfectly converge on training examples; test accuracy remains near chance and test predictions increasingly disagree while becoming more confident.
rows.note: Aggregate statement for 20 independently initialized models; the text gives no exact training accuracy or test-accuracy value.
rows.check: Separate training fit and chance test accuracy from prediction disagreement. Agreement across initializations alone does not establish accurate fitting; the paper also explicitly describes perfect random-label memorization.

rows.subject: 4×-width CNN ensemble (20 independently initialized models)
rows.size_stated: three convolutional layers with 128/256/512 channels and a 1024-unit hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Measure test predictions across random initializations after training on the same random labels.
rows.measure: Distribution of predicted test labels across random initializations
rows.value: Additional experiments confirmed that predicted labels on test examples are uniformly distributed when varying random initialization.
rows.note: The additional experiments are described as not shown; no numeric distribution is given.
rows.check: Uniform test predictions across initializations do not measure training-label fitting or directly establish test accuracy.

rows.subject: 4×-width CNN
rows.size_stated: three convolutional layers with 128/256/512 channels and a 1024-unit hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Train on natural CIFAR-10 images with random labels under fixed and fraction-scaled batch-size/learning-rate policies.
rows.value: All five fractions are memorized by the 4× model under both policies.
rows.note: Aggregate across five fractions for each of two policies; no per-fraction epoch values appear in the text.
rows.check: No substantive correction. The fraction-scaled policy changes batch size and learning rate across dataset sizes, but uses matched settings across label conditions at each size.

rows.subject: 4×-width CNN
rows.size_stated: three convolutional layers with 128/256/512 channels and a 1024-unit hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Train on natural CIFAR-10 images with true labels and random labels; measure epochs/presentations per example to 95% training accuracy.
rows.measure: Presentations per example to 95% training accuracy; fitted relation t95(n)=a+b/n
rows.baseline: true-label limiting value a approximately 10.3 presentations
rows.value: Random-label limiting value a approximately 34.7 presentations; fitted b values for true labels, random labels, and random pixels all lie in 7.2–7.8 × 104.
rows.note: The text says true-label training is consistently fastest and random labels are learned more slowly. The reported limits and relation show dataset-size dependence, but do not state a constant-factor training-time comparison.
rows.check: The fitted values permit a constant-factor comparison: 34.7/10.3 is approximately 3.37, and the fitted ratios over the measured dataset sizes are approximately 1.6–3.1. These are descriptive 95%-accuracy fits, not measured asymptotic limits or times to zero error. Dataset-size dependence does not contradict V2.

rows.subject: 4×-width CNN
rows.size_stated: three convolutional layers with 128/256/512 channels and a 1024-unit hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Train on natural CIFAR-10 images with random labels under the fraction-scaled policy; measure memorization threshold and completion.
rows.measure: Presentations per example to 95% training accuracy and completion of full memorization
rows.value: Presentations to 95% are reported as decreasing with dataset size across both policies; all five fractions are memorized under both policies.
rows.note: No exact per-fraction epoch counts are stated in the prose.
rows.check: Complete memorization supports V1. Changing dataset size does not test increasing label-corruption fractions, and this row provides no true-label timing comparison for V2. It duplicates the fraction-scaled portion of R3.

statements.problem: The approximate ratios are compatible with arithmetic from the reported quantities, but the paper does not report either ratio directly. The presentation ratios summarize fitted curves rather than stated per-fraction measurements.
